caption: Incident Macro F1 improved from the behavioral Random Forest baseline through XGBoost and K1 stacking, with the final sealed Holdout result remaining close to the fixed TRAIN reference.
Feature variant ablation separates behavioral-only evidence from CAIDA and RPKI/ROV enrichment effects before the later XGBoost and K1 phases.
Feature-family removal highlights which groups most affected grouped Macro F1 in the controlled TRAIN-only ablation.
Refined XGBoost improved Macro F1, Top-1, Top-2, and MRR relative to the refined Random Forest benchmark under the selected TRAIN-only comparison.
K1 temporal stacking materially improved incident-level classification over simple mean probability aggregation in the TRAIN-only K1 experiment.
K2 showed low seed sensitivity for the selected K1 architecture before the final deployable freeze.
The K2.5 architecture comparator supported keeping the XGBoost-to-XGBoost K1 design.
The frozen K1 model generalized strongly on the sealed Final Holdout, with high classification and ranking metrics.
Per-class Final Holdout metrics show strongest performance for Outage and the lowest F1 for Hijack.
The system ranked the true class first for 196 incidents and second for 15 incidents, yielding Top-2 coverage for 211 of 213 Final Holdout incidents.
The final confusion matrix shows most residual errors occur between Hijack and Leak, while Outage is sharply separated.
TRAIN-to-Holdout deltas are small for aggregate ranking metrics, with the largest class-specific difference in Hijack F1.
The final V4 feature corpus combines 44 behavioral, 14 CAIDA, and 16 RPKI/ROV features for 74 total model inputs.
